{ "title": "Getting Started with React 18 Hooks", "slug": "getting-started-react-18-hooks", "excerpt": "Learn how to use the latest React 18 hooks in your applications.", "data": "

React 18 introduced several new hooks that make state management and side effects easier to handle.

New Hooks Overview

1. useId Hook

The useId hook generates unique IDs that are stable across server and client rendering:

import { useId } from 'react';\n\nfunction MyComponent() {\n  const id = useId();\n  return <div id={id}>Unique content</div>;\n}

2. useTransition Hook

Mark updates as non-urgent to keep UI responsive:

import { useTransition, useState } from 'react';\n\nfunction SearchComponent() {\n  const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition();\n  const [query, setQuery] = useState('');\n  \n  const handleSearch = (value) => {\n    startTransition(() => {\n      setQuery(value);\n    });\n  };\n}

These hooks improve performance and user experience significantly.

", "status": "PUBLISHED", "language": "EN", "contentTypeId": 2, "tenantId": 2, "metaTitle": "React 18 Hooks Tutorial - Complete Guide", "metaDescription": "Complete guide to React 18 hooks including useId, useTransition, and performance optimization tips.", "metaKeywords": "react, hooks, javascript, tutorial, react18", "isFeatured": true, "template": "tutorial", "createdBy": 3, "publishedAt": "2024-01-20T10:00:00Z" }
